provenance.method: GB rail Passenger Assist route using regulator information; station/operator variability preserved.

question: How can I check passenger assistance for a train journey in Great Britain?
why_it_matters: People may need help planning, boarding, changing platforms or navigating disruption, and operator policies should be inspectable.
current_understanding: Licensed train and station operators have Accessible Travel Policies, and Passenger Assist can support people who need help because of disability, temporary impairment or age. Advance booking and turn-up-and-go both exist, but actual support depends on the station, operator, staffing and conditions. Check the specific journey.
evidence_needed: Stable operator-level cognitive/sensory accessibility metadata beyond physical-access fields.
reopening_conditions: ORR Passenger Assist standards or operator-policy requirements materially change.
dissent: Some travellers prefer not to pre-book; turn-up-and-go can increase flexibility but may be more dependent on conditions at the time.
